correctness.rationale: A direct invertible projection-plane mapping identifies the shadow hull with a base polygon plus Cauchy-distributed point. The full-vertex event is exactly one violated support inequality; for n>=5 each event cell is an explicit bounded triangle, and the probabilities are exact solid angles. A strictly increasing derivative-sign function H_n proves one global height maximum; substitution proves n=6 benchmark and controlled parameter limits yield the asymptotic coefficient. This covers all integers n>=5 and all h>0, with measure-zero exceptional directions excluded. The separately executed CHECK.py reconstructed 21,000 projected hulls and verified formula and asymptotic numerics.

value.rationale: Full-vertex retention under randomly oriented orthographic projection is a natural shape-visibility invariant. A geometry regime change at five base vertices produces bounded triangular visibility cells unlike known rectangular strips; sharp all-n height optimization, a closed hexagonal benchmark and n^-2 optimal retention law form a complete nontrivial classification for this family. Novelty is about these conclusions, not the standard solid-angle or Cauchy change-of-variables methods.
